newsitem.title: UK: IPE natgas untraded for fourth consecutive session.
newsitem.headline: IPE natgas untraded for fourth consecutive session.

text.p: The IPE natural gas futures contract was untraded on Tuesday morning for the fourth consecutive two-hour session. The last deal done on the exchange took place at 1039 GMT on Friday morning.
But brokers are not yet ready to read the last rites over the contract.
"Overall there's still a lot of things up in the air to do with deregulation in the industry," said a futures broker. "This reflects the ongoing deregulation process."

He added that if the contract is still as illiquid as this a year after the Interconnector pipeline from Bacton to Zeebrugge in Belgium opens, then there will be serious cause for concern, but this stage has not been reached yet.

A spokeswoman for the exchange said that the IPE has been in touch with the market to establish why trade has been so slow, and has found players still relatively relaxed. One view is that the OTC market has been busy recently, and with only a small group of players involved in the market, when the OTC market is busy they tend to leave the IPE alone.
The hope is that this situation can also work in reverse, so when the physical market quietens down, there may be a return to futures trading.
